validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #72 collects six follow-ups from the review and QA of PR #69 (for #42): five review findings and one QA-found defect. I re-derived every one against the current tree rather than accepting the report, and all six still hold.

TWO ARE REAL CODE DEFECTS.

(1) The forecast double-projects a posted-and-split schedule occurrence. generateForecast passes getTransactions' result to buildFutureScheduleOccurrences, and that query carries `.options({ splits: 'inline' })` (forecast-filters.ts:83). 'inline' appends `is_parent = 0` (aql/schema/executors.ts:238-244), which excludes split parents — and splitTransaction (shared/transactions.ts:386) leaves `schedule`/`schedule_occurrence` on the row it turns into a parent while makeChild (:57) copies neither onto the children. So the split parent is the ONE row carrying the occurrence stamp, and the forecast's row set cannot see it. isScheduleOccurrencePosted reports the occurrence unpaid and buildFutureScheduleOccurrences projects it a second time. I reproduced this by driving the real handlers (schedule/post-transaction, then splitTransaction + transactions-batch-update) against a weekly -10000 schedule: the occurrence's data point carried a projected -10000 and the 03-15 balance was -20000 against a -10000 control, and the row dump showed the stamp on the parent and null on both children. Display-only — it cannot double-pay, since that is the guard #69 fixed.

(2) Unsplitting a posted schedule payment destroys it. makeAsNonChildTransactions (shared/transactions.ts:439) decides to delete the parent from the CHILD COUNT (`remainingChildTransactions.length <= 1`) rather than from whether the children's amounts account for the parent. A split opened from the register starts as two 0.00 children (makeEmptySplitSubtransactions:85), so the count says 'safe' while the amounts say the parent is the only row holding any value — and the occurrence stamp with it. I called the function directly on a 12345 stamped parent with two 0.00 children: updated=[{amount:0},{amount:0}], deleted=[{amount:12345,schedule:'s1'}] — the payment and its stamp gone, and /schedules drops back to Due. The single-child branch at :452 already implements the correct behaviour; the general branch does not extend it.

TWO ARE DEFECTS IN #69's OWN TEST FILE. (3) The case 'leaves the status queries agreeing with the guard after a split' passes with the guard reverted — I removed `.options({ splits: 'all' })` from schedules/app.ts and got exactly 1 failed | 51 passed, the failure being its sibling 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split'. Its name and comment claim a direction it does not test. The guard direction IS covered by the sibling, so this is a framing gap, not missing coverage. (4) readSplitFamily's raw SQL against v_transactions_internal is justified in a comment that is false — I ran the AQL form against a real split and got all three rows back, with the occurrence as '2017-01-01' rather than the 20170102 integer the raw view forces the next assertion to work around.

TWO ARE PROCESS. (5) #69's title lacks the mandatory [AI] prefix. (6) #69's work order omitted its own release note from files[]. This order lists both notes.

plan/brief.md records no decisions and no prior rejection, so the issue text plus the repo's own PR rules are the only constraints. There is no 'Acceptance (from the split)' section in the issue, so no IAC-n needs tracing.
validated_work_order.root_cause:
Two independent defects sharing one shape: a consumer reads the (schedule, schedule_occurrence) stamp, or a transaction's amount, off a row set the default query shape cannot see.

The forecast reads the stamp off getTransactions' result, which passes splits:'inline' and therefore excludes split parents — the only rows carrying the stamp, since splitTransaction keeps schedule/schedule_occurrence on the row it makes a parent and makeChild copies neither onto children. The correct reader already exists and is already used three times: getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery (shared/schedules.ts:251) passes splits:'all' and returns exactly the ['schedule','date','schedule_occurrence'] shape indexPostedScheduleTransactions already expects. The forecast was the fourth reader and the only one on the default split type.

Unsplit: makeAsNonChildTransactions decides to delete the parent from the CHILD COUNT rather than from whether the children's amounts account for the parent. A register-made split has two 0.00 children, so the count says 'safe to delete' while the amounts say the parent is the only row carrying any value — and the occurrence stamp with it. The single-child branch at :452 already implements the correct behaviour; the general branch just does not extend it.
validated_work_order.approach:
Four code/test changes plus two release notes, each verified by execution on this tree before this order was written; every prototype was reverted and the working tree is clean.

A. FORECAST (finding 1). Stop deriving the forecast's occurrence state from getTransactions. In forecast/app.ts fetch `await aqlQuery(getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery(schedules))` after `schedules` is filtered and pass that to buildFutureScheduleOccurrences in place of `transactions`; retype that parameter to PostedScheduleTransaction[] (it reaches only indexPostedScheduleTransactions, so the wide TransactionEntity[] typing was looser than the use — and with a different row set behind it the narrow type is what stops a future caller reintroducing the bug). `transactions` still goes to projectForecastData untouched and must stay on the inline split set: there the CHILDREN carry the amounts the projection sums, which is exactly why the stamp cannot be read off it. I applied this and re-ran my reproduction — the projected entry on the occurrence's day disappeared, the 03-15 balance returned to -10000, the following week's occurrence still projected, and all 15 existing forecast tests plus the 24 in the forecast directory passed. `yarn typecheck` was green across all six workspaces.

B. UNSPLIT (finding 2). In makeAsNonChildTransactions, compute the children's total before the promote-and-delete result and narrow the existing `deleteParentTransaction` condition from the child count alone to the amounts: when at most one child would remain AND that total does not equal the parent's amount, return the parent as the sole surviving row through the existing makeTransactionWithChildCategory helper — which preserves schedule and schedule_occurrence — with the children as deleted. When the children do sum to the parent, the existing path is untouched. I prototyped this and exercised it over seven shapes: unfilled 2-child unsplit-all (the reported bug) now returns the 12345 stamped parent with both children deleted; FILLED 2-child still splits out into 5000 + 7345; partial 5000 + 0 keeps the parent; filled 3-child unselecting one still leaves the parent at 8345 with the promoted child alongside; 3-child unselecting two keeps the parent. Full loot-core suite with it applied: 87 files, 1268 passed, 1 expected fail, 2 skipped, exit 0.

C. TEST FRAMING (finding 3). Rename 'leaves the status queries agreeing with the guard after a split' to what it asserts — that the status queries still report a split-parented occurrence as posted — and replace its comment's guard-pinning claim with a pointer to the sibling that does pin it. No assertion changes.

D. TEST IDIOM (finding 4). Replace readSplitFamily's body with the AQL query, keeping the id/parent_id $or and selecting is_parent, parent_id, schedule_occurrence. The inline type literal, the internal view name and the 'read through AQL rather than off the raw view above' integer-date detour all go away. The justifying comment is deleted rather than rewritten, since its stated reason is false. I confirmed the AQL form returns all three rows with the occurrence already formatted.

E. RELEASE NOTES. Two notes, not one. The forecast correction folds into the existing schedule-occurrence note, which shares its root cause and symptom. The unsplit fix gets its own note (fix-unsplit-empty-split.md): it is NOT schedule-specific — unsplitting any split that was never filled in destroys the row's amount, in any account, schedule or not — so folding it into a note about schedule occurrences would misdescribe it. The proposal I am reviewing put both in one note; I split them because the second is a general register defect with its own audience.

I did not split the ticket. The two defects are two views of one interaction — what happens to a schedule payment once it has been split — and the unsplit fix is the wider-reaching while the forecast fix is a one-line argument change, so 'do the small one first' does not apply either. Reasoning in alternatives_considered.

files.change: Import getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery from '#shared/schedules' and aqlQuery from '#server/aql'. After `schedules` is filtered, fetch `const { data: postedScheduleTransactions } = await aqlQuery(getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery(schedules))` and pass it as the fifth argument to buildFutureScheduleOccurrences in place of `transactions`. `transactions` continues to projectForecastData unchanged — it must stay on the inline split set, because there the children carry the amounts the projection sums.
files.why: Fix for finding 1. getTransactions' inline split set cannot see a split parent, the only row carrying the occurrence stamp, so a posted-and-split occurrence is invisible to isScheduleOccurrencePosted and gets projected a second time. getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery already passes splits:'all' and returns exactly the three-column shape indexPostedScheduleTransactions expects.

files.change: Retype buildFutureScheduleOccurrences' `postedTransactions` parameter from TransactionEntity[] to PostedScheduleTransaction[] and import that type from '#shared/schedules'. No logic change — the array reaches only indexPostedScheduleTransactions, which has always been typed on PostedScheduleTransaction.
files.why: The parameter now receives a three-column projection rather than whole transaction rows. Typing it TransactionEntity[] would let a future caller pass the inline set back and silently reintroduce finding 1.

files.change: In makeAsNonChildTransactions, before the promote-and-delete result is computed, sum the children's amounts and narrow the parent's deletion from the child count alone to the amounts: when at most one child would remain (the existing deleteParentTransaction condition) AND that total does not equal the parent's amount, return the parent as the sole surviving row via the existing makeTransactionWithChildCategory helper — which preserves schedule and schedule_occurrence — with the children as deleted. When the children do sum to the parent, fall through to the existing path unchanged. Add a comment naming the invariant: a parent may only be deleted when the children account for it.
files.why: Fix for finding 2. Deletion is decided by remainingChildTransactions.length <= 1 alone, so a register-made split (two 0.00 children) makes the count say 'safe' while the amounts say the parent holds the only value and the occurrence stamp. The single-child branch at :452 already implements the correct behaviour; this generalises it to N children.

files.change: Comment only. The block at :586-597 explains that splits:'all' is required for the post guard and names getHasTransactionsQuery and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery as consumers that already pass it. Extend it to name the forecast as the fourth reader, now corrected.
files.why: No behaviour change — the guard itself is correct and was fixed by #69. A stale list of the correct readers is how the forecast reading drifted in the first place.

files.change: Two edits. (i) Rename the case 'leaves the status queries agreeing with the guard after a split' to 'still reports a split-parented occurrence as posted' and rewrite its comment to say what it asserts, pointing at the sibling 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split' as the case that pins the guard. No assertion changes. (ii) Replace the body of readSplitFamily with the AQL query: `q('transactions').options({ splits: 'all' }).filter({ $or: [{ id: parentId }, { parent_id: parentId }] }).select(['id', 'is_parent', 'parent_id', 'schedule_occurrence'])`. The inline DbViewTransactionInternal type literal and the v_transactions_internal reference go away, as does the 'read through AQL rather than off the raw view above, which stores the occurrence as a 20170102 integer' detour in the assertion below it. Delete the raw-SQL justification comment rather than rewriting it — its stated reason is false.
files.why: Fixes findings 3 and 4. A case whose name claims to pin the guard but passes with the guard reverted misleads the next reader about what is covered, and the raw-SQL helper hardcodes an internal view name that only executors.ts knows about.

files.change: Extend the existing note's body with one sentence covering the forecast correction: a schedule occurrence whose payment had been split was counted a second time as a future payment in the forecast. Keep the existing front matter (category: Bugfixes, authors: [Shivam-Fl]).
files.why: The forecast fix shares a root cause and one user-facing symptom with the split-occurrence fix. Finding 6 in reverse — #69's work order listed a release note that existed but omitted it from files[], so a reviewer re-derived that it was fine. This one is listed.

files.change: New release note. Front matter `category: Bugfixes` with an `authors` array; set the authors to whoever lands the PR, per packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md. Body, non-technical and one or two sentences: unsplitting a split you did not fill in used to delete the original transaction and leave empty rows behind; it now keeps the original transaction at its amount.
files.why: The unsplit fix is its own user-facing bugfix and is not schedule-specific — unsplitting any never-filled split destroys the row's amount, schedule or not. Folding it into a note about schedule occurrences would misdescribe it and bury it for users who never touched a schedule.

cases: does not re-project a posted occurrence whose transaction has been split — post a weekly schedule occurrence through the real handlers, split the posted row and give the two children half the amount each, assert the occurrence's data point has an empty `transactions` array and the running balance counts the real rows once. Today the point carries a projected entry of the full amount and the balance is 10000 too low from that date on.
keeps projecting the next occurrence after a split — control arm pinning that the fix removes the duplicate rather than all projection for a split-posted schedule.

unsplitting a split whose children were never filled in keeps the parent and its amount — 12345 stamped parent with two 0.00 children, unsplit both: one updated row at 12345, both children deleted, nothing at 0. The reproduced QA defect.

unsplitting that same parent leaves the occurrence stamp on the surviving row — the returned row still carries schedule and schedule_occurrence, which is what keeps /schedules reading Paid instead of Due. Asserted directly rather than inferred from the amount.

unsplitting a FILLED split still splits it out — 12345 parent with children 5000 and 7345, unsplit both: two updated children at their own amounts and the parent deleted. Guards against the fix over-reaching into correctly-filled splits.

unsplitting one child of a filled split still leaves the parent — 12345 parent with children 4000/4000/4345, unsplit the first: the parent survives at 8345 with the promoted child alongside and nothing deleted.

unsplitting two of three partially-typed children keeps the parent at its full amount — 12345 parent with children 5000/4000/0, unsplit the first two: the parent survives at 12345. This is the shape where the parent's amount and the typed partial amounts genuinely disagree, and it pins the rule this fix adopts so the choice is visible rather than incidental.

the existing case 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split' continues to pass and remains the one that fails when the guard's splits:'all' is reverted — the rename in finding 3 must not move that coverage onto the renamed case.

readSplitFamily reads the split family through AQL: the helper issues a q('transactions') query with splits:'all' and an $or over id/parent_id, and neither it nor the assertion below mentions v_transactions_internal or a 20170102 integer.

qa_script: Boot the demo budget via 'View demo' on the initial setup screen (after 'Don't use a server') — an empty budget has no schedules to exercise the schedule cases.

AC-3 first, since it is the one with visible data loss: add a one-off schedule (payee QA Unsplit Then Post, account Bank of America, amount 123.45, date a few days out). Post it from the row's actions menu ('Post transaction', not '…today'). In the register select the posted row, click its Category cell, choose Split, leave both new rows at 0.00. Right-click the split and choose 'Unsplit 1 transactions'. Expect the 123.45 row to remain standing alone with its schedule badge and the two 0.00 rows gone. Check /schedules: the occurrence must still read Paid and its preview row must be gone. Before the fix the 123.45 row disappears entirely, only the 0.00 rows remain, and /schedules reads Due with the preview row back.

AC-4 immediately after, on a split before it is unsplit: enter 50.00 and 73.45 into the two children, then 'Unsplit 1 transactions'. Expect two separate rows of 50.00 and 73.45 and no 123.45 parent — a filled split must still split out.

AC-1: add a weekly schedule on Checking for -100. Let one occurrence post, then split the posted register row and give the two children -50.00 each. Open the balance forecast over a window covering that occurrence and the next. Expect NO projected entry on the occurrence's day and the balance counting the real rows once; the following week's occurrence must still be projected. Before the fix a projected -100 sits on top of the real -100 and the balance is 100 too low.

The partially-typed case, which is the one to watch and is not in the ticket's repro: split a 123.45 row, type 50.00 into ONE child and leave the other empty, then unsplit both. Expect one row at 123.45 and the typed 50.00 gone. That is the rule this fix adopts and it is a visible change; confirm it, and report it in the PR description rather than letting a reviewer find it.

AC-7 and AC-8 at PR time: confirm the PR title begins with '[AI] ', and that both upcoming-release-notes/fix-unsplit-empty-split.md and the edited fix-split-occurrence-double-post.md appear in files[] along with every other changed path.

alternatives_considered.approach: Change getTransactions in forecast-filters.ts to pass splits:'all' so the forecast can see the split parent.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the symptom by breaking the balance projection. That query's inline split set is load-bearing: projectForecastData sums the CHILDREN's amounts, because the parent is not additive with them. Widening it double-counts every split — the existing test 'does not double-count split parents in posted transaction balances' is exactly that guard, and it passed with the fix as proposed. The two consumers need opposite split types, so they need separate queries.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add splits:'all' only for the schedule-occurrence columns, by selecting them off a second filtered query rather than reusing getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The query already exists, already passes splits:'all', and already returns exactly the ['schedule','date','schedule_occurrence'] shape the consumers are typed on. A variant means a second place that must remember the splits rule — which is how the forecast drifted in the first place.

alternatives_considered.approach: For the unsplit defect, carry the parent's residual onto one of the promoted children instead of keeping the parent.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It must invent a rule for which child absorbs the difference, and produces two rows where the user had one transaction. The function already has the right answer one branch above — the single-child case keeps the parent at its own amount; generalising it invents nothing.

alternatives_considered.approach: For the unsplit defect, refuse the unsplit outright when the children do not sum to the parent, surfacing an error.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Unsplitting is a user-initiated revert of a split they made moments earlier, and the register already shows the split error on the row. Blocking moves the problem rather than fixing it and leaves the count-vs-amount decision in place.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 3, add `await post(id)` after the split in the 'status queries agreeing' case so it pins the guard, rather than renaming it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is a framing gap, not missing coverage: the sibling already pins the guard and fails when it is reverted, which I confirmed by running it. A second copy duplicates coverage in the same file for no new signal.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the unsplit defect in the desktop-client caller (Account.tsx onMakeAsNonSplitTransactions) rather than in makeAsNonChildTransactions.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That puts the invariant in the one UI that happens to call it today, at the wrong layer: the function is what decides a parent is safe to delete. I checked the callers — the only production call sites are Account.tsx:1242 and :1266, both inside onMakeAsNonSplitTransactions, and the api package does not reach it — but the caller does not know the amounts and the function does.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fold the unsplit fix's release note into the existing schedule-occurrence note, as the reviewed proposal did, on the grounds that both fixes share a root cause and one symptom.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The root cause and symptom are shared between the forecast fix and the split-occurrence fix, not between those and the unsplit fix. Unsplitting a never-filled split destroys the amount of any register row, schedule or not, and the schedule is only how QA happened to hit it. One note titled for schedule occurrences would misdescribe a general register defect and hide it from users who never used a schedule. Two notes, both listed in files[].

alternatives_considered.approach: Split the ticket: one work order for the forecast finding, another for the unsplit finding, deferring the two test-file findings to a docs-only change.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The two defects are two views of the same interaction — what happens to a schedule payment once it has been split — and both end in the occurrence being miscounted. They are not separable by risk either: the unsplit fix is the wider-reaching and the forecast fix is a one-line argument change, so 'do the small one first' does not apply. Splitting would also mean two PRs racing on the same test files. The files[] entries group the work cleanly enough to lift out if a maintainer disagrees.

risks: The unsplit change alters a shared helper used by every 'Unsplit' action in the register, not only the schedule case QA reported. The guard is deliberately narrow — it only fires when the children do not account for the parent, so a filled split is untouched — and the full 1268-test loot-core suite passed with it applied, but this is the widest-reaching change in the order and deserves the reviewer's attention first.

The unsplit fix changes what the user sees after an action they expected to expand a split. A user who split a row, typed amounts into some children, then unsplit now gets one row at the parent's amount rather than rows at the children's amounts. That is the intended correction — current behaviour silently loses money — but it is visible on a common action and must be called out in the PR description, not just the release note.

Adding a fifth AQL query to generateForecast is a real cost on a hot path refetched on every account or filter change. The added query is schedule-scoped and unbounded by date, mirroring what useSchedules already runs; on a budget with many schedules it reads more rows than the old path. I verified correctness, not latency. If latency shows up the follow-up is to narrow it by the same account ids, not to revert to reading the stamp off getTransactions.
The forecast fix is display-only — it cannot double-pay, that is the guard #69 fixed — but it changes balances users have been shown, so cached or screenshot-compared forecast figures will move.
The comment edit in schedules/app.ts lands in a file the guard fix already touched. Comment-only, but it appears in a diff a reviewer is reading closely.
out_of_scope: Retitling PR #69 to carry the [AI] prefix. It is a one-word change to a merged PR's title, not a code change, so it cannot appear in files[], and editing another PR's title is outward-facing. The rule in .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md is unambiguous and the omission is systemic across 71, 68, 67 and 65 — recorded in residual_risks so it is not silently dropped, and whoever holds write access can do it in one command. This PR's own title is covered by AC-7.

Making the schedule stamp survive an unsplit by re-stamping the promoted children. The fix keeps the parent instead, preserving the stamp without inventing one on rows that never carried it. Re-stamping would let a split-out payment keep its occurrence identity — a design question about what the stamp means, not a follow-up to this defect.

E2E coverage for the unsplit path. There is no Playwright test for the register's 'Unsplit' action today. The unit cases plus the browser checks in qa_script cover the reported defect; adding e2e coverage is separate work.
The other consumers of getTransactions. Fixing the split reading here leaves the forecast's other inline-split uses exactly as they were, deliberately: they are balance uses and want the children.

Whether the forecast should itemise a split-parented occurrence's children as separate projected rows rather than suppressing the projection. The children are real amounts the register already shows; whether the forecast ought to show them per child is a product question this order does not raise.

Ran the reviewer's AQL form against a real split: `q('transactions').options({ splits: 'all' }).filter({ $or: [{ id: parentId }, { parent_id: parentId }] }).select(['id', 'is_parent', 'parent_id', 'schedule_occurrence'])` returned all three rows — parent is_parent true with schedule_occurrence '2017-01-01', both children is_parent false, parent_id set, occurrence null. The raw view returned the same three rows with the occurrence as the integer 20170101, which is the detour the next assertion has to route around. AQL declares parent_id at aql/schema/index.ts:39 and schedule_occurrence at :56.

Arbiter caller sweep for makeAsNonChildTransactions: the only production call sites are packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Account.tsx:1242 and :1266, both inside onMakeAsNonSplitTransactions; the only other references are the unit test and a generated @types declaration. packages/api does not reach it.

Arbiter check of the proposal's one soft spot. The proposal claims its rule 'stops amount loss in every shape'. I tested a shape its test list does not cover — a 12345 parent with children 5000/4000/0, unselecting two — and the rule keeps the parent at 12345 while discarding the 9000 of typed partial amounts. Current code instead keeps 9000 and loses 7345. Neither shape is lossless because the parent's amount and the typed amounts genuinely disagree; the rule trades the user's typed amounts for the parent's full amount. That is a defensible choice, it is what the existing single-child branch does, and it is now pinned by an explicit test case and called out in qa_script rather than left implicit.
assumptions: That the children's amounts are the authority for whether a split has been 'filled in' is the semantics the single-child branch at shared/transactions.ts:452 already implements, and it matches QA's stated Expected. If the intended behaviour for a partially-filled split is instead to keep the partial amounts and drop the parent, the condition must narrow to a children-sum-of-zero test — and I would want that decided before merge rather than after, because it is the one shape where this change is visible and lossy.

That unsplitting a never-filled split should restore the original single transaction, discarding the empty children's zero amounts, rather than producing N zero rows. QA's Expected states this directly, but it is a product judgement, not derivable from the code.

That no other caller depends on makeAsNonChildTransactions deleting a parent whose children do not sum to it. I swept every caller: the only production call sites are Account.tsx:1242 and :1266 (both the 'Unsplit' menu action) and the api package does not reach it.

That the forecast's `transactions` set must keep its inline splits for the balance projection. I read projectForecastData, summarizePostedTransactions, and the guard test 'does not double-count split parents in posted transaction balances'. The passing test corroborates this but does not prove it for every code path.

That passing PostedScheduleTransaction[] rather than TransactionEntity[] into buildFutureScheduleOccurrences is a type-level clarification, not a behaviour change. I read the body end to end: the array reaches only indexPostedScheduleTransactions, which reads schedule, date and schedule_occurrence.

That the unsplit fix warrants its own release note rather than extending the schedule-occurrence note. My reasoning is in alternatives_considered; a maintainer who prefers one combined note can merge the two bodies, but the slug and audience should not imply the unsplit bug is schedule-only.

That the implementation agent has, or can obtain, the GitHub author handle for the new release note's `authors` key. packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md asks for the usernames of the people who contributed the PR.
unknowns: Whether the partially-typed split case (some children typed, sum short of the parent) has a settled product answer distinct from the never-filled one. The code does not say which is intended. I adopted the rule that keeps the parent's full amount and discards the typed partials, because it matches the existing single-child branch and stops the more severe loss, but this is the one place a maintainer may want to overrule the plan — and unlike the reviewed proposal's account of it, I have verified that this shape loses real money on both sides of the change rather than only on one.

Whether unsplitting a filled split where the children sum to the parent but the parent itself carries an occurrence stamp is exercised anywhere in the e2e suite. I found no e2e coverage for the unsplit path at all, which is why AC-3 and AC-4 are verified in a browser as well as by unit test.

Whether the forecast is the only remaining consumer reading the stamp off an inline split set. I enumerated the readers by grepping isScheduleOccurrencePosted, indexPostedScheduleTransactions, getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery and getHasTransactionsQuery across packages/; the guard, the two status queries and the forecast are all of them, and desktop-client's useSchedules hook uses getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery. I could not rule out a reader that queries the stamp column directly without going through those helpers.

The exact behaviour of the register's Category-cell split affordance versus the right-click 'Unsplit 1 transactions' item when a split has more than two children. QA's repro and my fixtures both use two; the three-child path is covered only by the proposed unit tests, not by a browser check.
validated_work_order.debate_summary:
There was no debate to arbitrate: plan/critique.json is an empty object. The critic produced nothing, so there are no findings to sustain or dismiss, and I did not manufacture agreement with a position that was never taken. What I did instead was re-derive all six findings myself, by execution on this tree rather than by reading the report, because an empty critique leaves the proposal unexamined and an unexamined plan is not a checked one.

All six hold. I reproduced both code defects independently of the proposal's evidence and by a different route: the forecast case driven through the real post-transaction and batch-update handlers rather than by inserting rows, and the unsplit case by calling makeAsNonChildTransactions directly. I then applied both proposed fixes, confirmed the forecast's projected entry and the 10000 balance error disappear while the following occurrence still projects, confirmed the unsplit fix across seven row shapes, and ran the full 1268-test loot-core suite and a six-workspace typecheck green. I reverted every prototype; the tree is clean.

I also re-verified the two test-file findings by running the disproofs rather than accepting them: reverting the guard's splits:'all' gave 1 failed | 51 passed with the failure in the sibling and the 'status queries agreeing' case passing, which is exactly the framing gap claimed; and the AQL form returned all three split-family rows with the occurrence as '2017-01-01' rather than the 20170102 integer, confirming the raw SQL's justification is false.

Two things I changed rather than accepted. First, the proposal folds both fixes into the existing schedule-occurrence release note on the grounds that they share a root cause and a symptom. That is true of the forecast fix and false of the unsplit fix: unsplitting a never-filled split destroys the amount of any register row, and the schedule is only how QA happened to find it. I split it into a second note with a schedule-agnostic slug, because one note titled for schedule occurrences would misdescribe a general register defect. Second, the proposal claims its unsplit rule 'stops amount loss in every shape' and treats the partially-typed case as a minor open question. I tested a shape its tests do not cover — a 12345 parent with children 5000/4000/0 — and found the rule keeps 12345 while discarding 9000 of typed amounts, against current code keeping 9000 and losing 7345. Both lose money because the parent's amount and the typed amounts genuinely disagree; the proposal's account of this shape was one-sided, and it is the one case where this change is visible and lossy. I kept the rule (it matches the existing single-child branch and stops the more severe loss) but pinned it with an explicit test case, put it in qa_script to be reported in the PR description, and said plainly in residual_risks that this is the place a maintainer may overrule the plan.

What I did not do is split the ticket, agreeing with the proposal and for its reasons plus one of its own: the unsplit fix is the wider-reaching change and the forecast fix is a one-line argument change, so the usual 'do the small one first' argument for separating them does not apply, and two PRs would race on the same test files. The route is plan -> implement -> review -> qa, and the review stage is the right place for the shared-helper change, so I am not requesting a stage.
residual_risks: The partially-typed split semantics are a product judgement, not a derivation from the code, and this is where the change is both visible and lossy. If a maintainer decides the typed partial amounts should win and the parent should go, the condition narrows to a children-sum-of-zero test and nothing else in the order moves. Both options lose money in that shape because the parent's amount and the typed amounts disagree; I have measured both (fix: 12345 survives, 9000 typed is discarded; current: 9000 survives, 7345 is lost) and put the case in qa_script so it is checked and reported rather than discovered.

The unsplit fix's guard fires on child count as well as amount, so unsplitting a subset of children from a never-filled split deletes the children the user did not select as well. I verified the money outcome is right (the parent survives at its full amount) but this dissolves the whole split rather than only the selected children. That follows from keeping the parent as the sole surviving row, and it is the behaviour the reported QA case expects; it is worth a reviewer confirming it reads as intentional.

The added AQL query on the forecast's hot path is unmeasured. I verified correctness, not latency; the schedule-scoped query mirrors what useSchedules already runs, but a budget with many schedules may read more rows than the old path did.
The release note split is a judgement call that a maintainer may reverse by merging the two note bodies. AC-8 then becomes a wording check rather than a second file.

The caller sweep covered packages/ excluding node_modules; a consumer reaching makeAsNonChildTransactions through a generated or dynamic import path would not have appeared in it, though the generated @types declaration is the only non-source reference I found.

The [AI] prefix omission is systemic across pipeline-authored PRs 65, 67, 68, 69 and 71, not specific to this ticket. Retitling #69 is one command for someone with write access, but nothing here fixes the pipeline that produced the other four.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Both defects reproduce under my own testing rather than on the proposal's word, both fixes were applied and measured (the forecast fix against a reproduction I built independently and against the full forecast suite plus a six-workspace typecheck; the unsplit fix against seven row shapes plus the full 1268-test loot-core suite), and the two test-file findings were each confirmed by running their disproof — reverting the guard, and running the AQL form the reviewer proposed. Caller sweeps confirmed the blast radius is the register's Unsplit action only. What holds the number below the high 80s is the partially-typed split: I measured it and it loses money on both sides of the change, the parent's amount and the typed amounts genuinely disagree and the code does not say which the user meant, so the rule I inherited is a defensible product judgement rather than a derivation. That judgement is now pinned by a test and flagged to QA and the PR description rather than left implicit, which is why I did not go lower. Smaller deductions: the added AQL query on the forecast's hot path is unmeasured for latency, and the unsplit fix's guard dissolves a whole split when the user unsplits only some of its children — the money is right, but that reading deserves a reviewer's confirmation.
